name: Holden
overview: General Motors-Holden (GM-H) was Australia's definitive domestic automaker and cultural icon. Emerging from an Adelaide saddlery founded by James Alexander Holden in 1856 and later coachbuilding giant Holden's Motor Body Builders (HMBB), Holden partnered with General Motors in 1931 and launched Australia's first mass-produced domestic motor vehicle, the 48-215 (popularly FX), on 29 November 1948. For seven decades, Holden engineered and manufactured vehicles tailored specifically to Australia's vast distances, harsh corrugated roads, and extreme climates at primary assembly complexes in Fishermans Bend and Dandenong (Victoria), Elizabeth and Woodville (South Australia), Pagewood (New South Wales), Acacia Ridge (Queensland), and Mosman Park (Western Australia). From the ubiquitous Kingswood, Monaro, and Torana to the legendary Commodore and luxury Statesman/Caprice, Holden shaped the Australian national identity, dominated Australian motorsport including multiple Bathurst 1000 victories, and exported vehicles across North America, the Middle East, South Africa, and New Zealand before local manufacturing ceased at Elizabeth on 20 October 2017 and the brand retired in 2020.
australian_history:
Holden's origins trace to 1856 when English immigrant James Alexander Holden established J.A. Holden & Co., a saddlery and leather goods business in Adelaide, South Australia. By 1917, under grandson Edward Wheewall Holden, wartime chassis import restrictions spurred the founding of Holden's Motor Body Builders Ltd (HMBB), which quickly became the Southern Hemisphere's largest coachbuilder, supplying bodies for GM, Ford, Chrysler, and Studebaker. In 1931, General Motors acquired HMBB to form General Motors-Holden's Ltd (GM-H). Under wartime Prime Minister Ben Chifley's post-WWII call for an Australian-built car, GM-H embarked on 'Project 2000' led by Laurence Hartnett. On 29 November 1948, Chifley famously unveiled the Holden 48-215 (later known as the FX) with the immortal words: 'She's a beauty!'.

Throughout the 1950s and 1960s, Holden held over 50% market share with the FJ (1953), the modern FE and FC series, and the breakthrough 1963 EH Holden, which introduced the ultra-reliable Red motor (149ci and 179ci) and sold over 250,000 units in 18 months. In 1968, Holden introduced the full-size HK series, introducing the iconic Kingswood nameplate, the pillarless Monaro sports coupe (which won the 1968 Bathurst 500 on debut with Bruce McPhee), and Holden's first locally designed and manufactured V8 engines (the 253ci and 308ci Red V8s cast at Fishermans Bend). The compact HB/LC/LJ Torana line cemented Holden's racing pedigree through Peter Brock and the Holden Dealer Team (HDT), achieving legendary status with the triple-carburettor LJ GTR XU-1 and the V8-powered LH/LX SL/R 5000 and A9X options.

In 1977, Holden pioneered Radial Tuned Suspension (RTS), transforming Australian handling dynamics across the HZ and Torana lineups. The oil crises of the 1970s prompted Holden to downsize from the traditional full-size Kingswood platform to a European-derived mid-size architecture, resulting in the launch of the VB Commodore in October 1978. Based on an Opel Rekord/Senator foundation but comprehensively re-engineered with 35% heavier body stiffening and rugged Australian suspension, the Commodore went on to become Australia's best-selling car for 15 consecutive years (1996-2010). Under the Australian Federal Government's Button Car Plan in the late 1980s, GM-H formed the United Australian Automobile Industries (UAAI) joint venture with Toyota, producing badge-engineered models including the Nova (Corolla) and Apollo (Camry) until 1996.

In 2006, Holden achieved its engineering pinnacle with the VE Commodore, a $1.03 billion ground-up Australian development on GM's global rear-wheel-drive Zeta platform. The Zeta platform also spawned the long-wheelbase WM Statesman/Caprice and underpinned exported vehicles including the Pontiac G8, Chevrolet SS, and Chevrolet Caprice Police Pursuit Vehicle (PPV) in the United States. Following the global financial crisis, shifting consumer preferences toward compact SUVs, the soaring Australian dollar, and escalating manufacturing cost pressures, General Motors announced in December 2013 that it would cease manufacturing in Australia. On 20 October 2017, the final Australian-built Holden—a Red Hot VF Series II Commodore SS-V Redline sedan—rolled off the Elizabeth assembly line in South Australia. Holden transitioned briefly to an all-import lineup, including the European Opel-sourced ZB Commodore and US-sourced Acadia and Equinox SUVs, before General Motors retired the historic Holden marque permanently at the end of 2020.

models.name: Holden Commodore
models.overview: The Holden Commodore was Australia's definitive full-size passenger car, holding the crown as the nation's best-selling car for 15 consecutive years (1996-2010). Spanning 16 distinct series codes across five generations from the original 1978 VB to the billion-dollar Australian-engineered VE/VF Zeta platform and the imported European ZB, the Commodore was the family hauler, police highway patrol interceptor, commercial utility, and Mount Panorama Bathurst racing champion for over four decades.

models.name: Holden Kingswood / Belmont / Premier
models.vehicle_type: Sedan / Wagon / Utility / Panel Van / Cab Chassis
models.overview: The Holden Kingswood was Australia's definitive full-size family car and commercial workhorse from 1968 to 1985. Replacing the HR series with the all-new HK, the Kingswood moniker became an indelible piece of Australian cultural lexicon—celebrated in television ('Kingswood Country'), song, and outback folklore. Encompassing the budget Belmont, mainstream Kingswood, luxury Premier, sporty Monaro-derived options, surf-culture Sandman van/ute, and heavy-duty One Tonner cab-chassis, over 1.5 million examples were produced across HK, HT, HG, HQ, HJ, HX, HZ, and WB series.

models.name: Holden Astra
models.overview: Spanning 36 years across seven generations, the Holden Astra was Holden's frontline small car. Launched in August 1984 as the LB/LC Astra, it originated as a badge-engineered Nissan Pulsar assembled in Clayton, Victoria. Under the Button Car Plan, the 1987 LD Astra combined Nissan body engineering with Holden's locally manufactured 1.6L and 1.8L Family II engines. In 1996, the Astra was reborn as the TR series, imported from Opel in Europe. The 1998 TS Astra became a massive commercial triumph, winning Wheels Car of the Year and spawning the hot hatch SRi and SRi Turbo (147 kW). The 2004 AH brought dynamic European styling and the 177 kW Astra VXR, followed by the PJ VXR coupe and the final high-tech 2016-2020 BK Astra hatchback (European Car of the Year) before Holden's retirement.

models.name: Holden EJ / EH / HD / HR
models.vehicle_type: Sedan / Station Sedan / Utility / Panel Van
models.overview: The 1962-1968 era represents the golden age of 1960s Holden dominance. The July 1962 EJ introduced clean, modern European-inspired styling, the milestone 1,000,000th Holden produced, and the prestigious Premier luxury model with standard automatic, leather bucket seats, and metallic paint. In August 1963, the legendary EH debuted Holden's all-new, world-class 'Red Motor' inline-six—featuring a 7-bearing crankshaft, hydraulic lifters, and 149ci (2.4L) and 179ci (2.9L) capacities. The EH became Australia's fastest-selling car ever, selling over 250,000 units in 18 months and claiming podium fame at Mount Panorama with the EH S4 Bathurst homologation special. The 1965 HD brought wider passenger accommodations and the twin-carburettor X2 engine, while the April 1966 HR resolved styling with crisp modern lines, front disc brakes, wider track, and the 186S engine with twin-barrel Bendix-Stromberg WW carburettor.

models.name: Holden Cruze
models.overview: The Holden Cruze nameplate lived two major chapters in Australia. First launched from 2002 to 2006 as the YG Cruze, it was an innovative subcompact all-wheel-drive crossover co-developed with Suzuki (based on the Ignis) featuring elevated ground clearance and 1.5L power. In 2009, Holden revived the name with the JG Cruze sedan. Most significantly, from March 2011 until October 2016, Holden invested over $1 billion to manufacture the JH Cruze Series II locally on a dedicated assembly line alongside the Commodore at Elizabeth, South Australia. The Australian-built Cruze featured an Australian-designed 5-door hatchback body style, local steering and suspension tuning, high-spec SRi and SRi-V turbo models (1.4L and 1.6L 132 kW turbos), and an efficient 2.0L Turbo Diesel. Over 125,000 Cruzes were built at Elizabeth.

models.name: Holden Sandman
models.overview: The Holden Sandman is the undisputed emblem of 1970s Australian youth and beach culture. Introduced in January 1974 on the HQ series (option package XX7 / XU3), the Sandman transformed humble commercial panel vans and utilities into vibrant, psychedelic recreational machines. Featuring bold side stripes, Monaro GTS sports dashboard with tachometer, GTS steering wheel, slotted steel rally wheels, twin bucket seats, and standard or optional 253ci and 308ci Red V8 power, the Sandman became a pop-culture legend closely tied to surfing, drive-in cinemas, and Australian freedom. The Sandman package carried through the HQ, HJ, HX, and HZ series until 1980, with authentic surviving examples now among Australia's most fiercely sought-after collector cars.

models.name: Holden Adventra & Crewman
models.vehicle_type: All-Wheel-Drive Cross Wagon / Dual-Cab Utility / Cab Chassis
models.overview: Developed during Holden's multi-million dollar engineering expansion under the VY/VZ Commodore program, the Adventra and Crewman represented audacious Australian engineering innovations. The 2003 Crewman was Australia's first locally designed and manufactured monocoque dual-cab utility, seating five adults on an extended 3,200 mm wheelbase with a heavy-duty leaf-sprung live rear axle capable of carrying up to a tonne. The Adventra was Holden's crossover all-wheel-drive sport wagon, boasting an Australian-engineered 'Cross-Trac' permanent AWD system (62% rear, 38% front torque split with automatic brake-traction management) and raised ground clearance. Holden combined the two concepts to create the monstrous Crewman Cross 8 and Cross 6, alongside V8 SS performance dual-cabs.

models.name: Holden FE / FC / FB / EK
models.vehicle_type: Sedan / Station Sedan / Utility / Panel Van
models.overview: The second and third generation post-war Holdens represented major leaps forward in Australian automotive engineering and design. Launched in July 1956, the FE introduced a completely modern, longer, lower body with wrap-around windscreen, 12-volt electrical architecture, recirculating ball steering, and Holden's very first factory station wagon—marketed as the 'Station Sedan'. The May 1958 FC refined the formula with an egg-crate grille and became the first car in Australian history to sell over 100,000 units in a calendar year. In January 1960, the FB adopted American fin-tail styling and a larger 138ci Grey motor, followed in May 1961 by the EK, which brought the historic introduction of the 3-speed Hydra-Matic automatic transmission to Holden. Across all four series, over 740,000 vehicles were built.

models.name: Holden Torana
models.overview: The Holden Torana (derived from an Aboriginal word meaning 'to fly') is one of Australian motorsport's greatest legends. Starting in 1967 as a modified Vauxhall Viva four-cylinder compact (HB), the Torana evolved into a giant-killing six-cylinder weapon in the LC and LJ series, highlighted by Peter Brock's rainy 1972 Bathurst 500 victory in the triple-carburettor LJ GTR XU-1. The LH and LX generations made Australian automotive history as the only car platform engineered to accommodate 4-, 6-, and 8-cylinder engines, culminating in the Bathurst-dominating SL/R 5000 and A9X option pack.

models.name: Holden Monaro
models.overview: The Holden Monaro is Australia's most revered two-door muscle car and grand tourer. Introduced in July 1968 with the HK series, the pillarless hardtop coupe captured national imagination by winning the 1968 Bathurst 500 on debut with Bruce McPhee and Barry Mulholland in a GTS 327, followed by Colin Bond's win in the 1969 HT GTS 350. Resurrected thirty-three years later following a sensational reception as the 'Coupe 22' concept at the 1998 Sydney Motor Show, the modern V2 and VZ Monaro CV8 captivated enthusiasts globally and was exported to North America as the Pontiac GTO and the UK as the Vauxhall Monaro.

models.name: Holden Statesman / Caprice
models.overview: The Holden Statesman and Caprice was Australia's presidential luxury flagship for nearly five decades. Conceived to challenge the Ford Fairlane and LTD, the Statesman rode on an extended 114-inch to 118-inch wheelbase providing unmatched rear legroom. Serving as official transport for Australian prime ministers, diplomats, business executives, and luxury hire car fleets, the Statesman and Caprice evolved from the ornate HQ-WB models to the modern IRS-equipped VQ-WL series and the billion-dollar Zeta-platform WM and WN. Exported globally as the Chevrolet Caprice, Buick Park Avenue, and US Police Pursuit Vehicle (PPV).

models.name: Holden 48-215 (FX)
models.overview: The Holden 48-215 (retrospectively referred to as the 'FX') was Australia's first mass-produced domestic motor vehicle, famously unveiled on 29 November 1948 by Prime Minister Ben Chifley with the words: 'She's a beauty!'. Developed under GM Project 2000, it combined American interior room and robust unibody construction with European operating economy, tailored specifically for Australia's harsh corrugated roads. In January 1951, the 50-2106 Coupe Utility was launched, defining the iconic Australian 'ute', followed in July 1953 by the 48-215-257 Business Sedan for taxi operators. Over 120,402 examples were produced.

models.name: Holden FJ
models.overview: Launched in October 1953, the Holden FJ is Australia's most recognized cultural automotive icon of the 1950s. Featuring an assertive horizontal chrome tooth grille, redesigned torpedo rear styling, and the introduction of the luxurious 'Special' sedan badge with two-tone leather options, the FJ captured 50% of Australian new car registrations. In December 1953, the iconic FJ Panel Van was introduced, creating the quintessential Aussie tradesman vehicle. The FJ was also Holden's first exported model, shipped to New Zealand in 1954. Total production reached 169,969 units.

models.name: Holden Gemini
models.overview: The Holden Gemini was Australia's best-selling four-cylinder car of the 1970s and early 1980s. Developed from GM's global T-car platform (shared with the Opel Kadett C, Isuzu Bellett Gemini, and Chevrolet Chevette), the Gemini won the prestigious 1975 Wheels Car of the Year award on debut. Over 226,000 units were produced across TX, TC, TD, TE, TF, and TG rear-wheel-drive series before transitioning to the front-wheel-drive RB series.

models.name: Holden Sunbird

models.name: Holden Brougham

models.name: Holden Rodeo
models.vehicle_type: Ute / Cab Chassis / Space Cab / Crew Cab 4x2 & 4x4
models.overview: For nearly three decades from 1980 to 2008, the Holden Rodeo was one of Australia's most trusted commercial workhorses and outback touring utilities. Engineered by Isuzu Motors and sold through Holden dealerships across Australia, the Rodeo spanned the tough KB series (1980-1988), the long-running TF series (1988-2003, famous for its bulletproof 2.8L 4JB1-T turbo-diesel and 3.2L V6), and the redesigned RA series (2003-2008). The Rodeo pioneered crew-cab four-wheel-drive dual-cab versatility in Australia, proving equally adept on cattle stations, mining sites, and suburban driveways before being renamed Colorado in 2008.

models.name: Holden Barina
models.overview: For over 33 years across six generations, the Holden Barina was Australia's quintessential light car. Introduced in February 1985 as the MB Barina (a badge-engineered Suzuki Cultus made unforgettable by poet Pam Ayres' commercial: 'Beep beep, Barina!'), the model transitioned through the ML, MF, and MH series. In 1994, Holden pivoted to GM Europe with the SB Barina (Opel Corsa B), creating an Australian youth lifestyle phenomenon that produced the cult Barina GSi (1.6L 16V twin-cam). The 2001 XC Barina won Wheels Car of the Year 2001. Sourcing moved to GM Daewoo in 2005 with the value-focused TK, while the final 2011-2018 TM Barina featured GM's global Gamma II platform, culminating in the sporty Barina RS powered by a 103 kW 1.4L Turbo engine.

models.name: Holden Captiva
models.overview: The Holden Captiva was Holden's core mid-size family SUV between 2006 and 2018, competing in Australia's exploding SUV segment against the Ford Territory and Toyota Kluger. Built on GM's global Theta platform, the range uniquely comprised two distinct body styles: the 5-seater Captiva 5 (Opel Antara twin) and the 7-seater Captiva 7 (Chevrolet Captiva). Over 150,000 Captivas found homes in Australian driveways thanks to keen pricing, standard three-row seating, AWD capability, and Australian-built Alloytec 3.2L and 3.0L SIDI V6 engines alongside 2.0L and 2.2L common-rail turbo diesels. Series II arrived in 2011 with refreshed styling, before the model was replaced by the Equinox and Acadia.

models.name: Holden Jackaroo
models.overview: The Holden Jackaroo (Isuzu Trooper / Bighorn) was Holden's frontline heavy-duty four-wheel-drive wagon from 1981 to 2004. Engineered to conquer the Australian outback, the Jackaroo competed directly against the Toyota LandCruiser Prado, Mitsubishi Pajero, and Nissan Patrol. The first-generation UBS-1 (1981-1992) offered short and long wheelbase bodies with rugged four-cylinder petrol and diesel engines. The second-generation UBS-2 (1992-2004) expanded into a wide-body luxury family 4WD featuring coil-sprung rear suspension, shift-on-the-fly 4WD, potent 3.2L and 3.5L DOHC 24V V6 petrol engines (158 kW), and advanced 3.0L 4JX1 common-rail turbo-diesel. The flagship Monterey added leather trim, woodgrain, climate control, and heated seats.

models.name: Holden Colorado
models.overview: The Holden Colorado was Holden's rugged 4x4 and 4x2 dual-cab, space-cab, and single-cab workhorse pick-up, replacing the legendary Rodeo in 2008. Across the RC and RG generations, the Colorado delivered class-leading 3.5-tonne braked towing capacity and up to 500Nm of torque from its Duramax 2.8L turbo-diesel engine. In 2016, Holden's engineering team at Lang Lang conducted a massive Australian-specific chassis, steering, and powertrain calibration that transformed refinement and dynamics.

commodore.overview: The Holden Commodore was Australia's definitive full-size passenger car, holding the crown as the nation's best-selling car for 15 consecutive years (1996-2010). Spanning 16 distinct series codes across five generations from the original 1978 VB to the billion-dollar Australian-engineered VE/VF Zeta platform and the imported European ZB, the Commodore was the family hauler, police highway patrol interceptor, commercial utility, and Mount Panorama Bathurst racing champion for over four decades.
commodore.australian_market_notes: First conceived in response to the 1973 oil crisis as a smaller, more fuel-efficient alternative to the full-size Kingswood, Holden heavily re-engineered the German Opel Rekord/Senator body with 35% heavier structural reinforcement, MacPherson strut front suspension, four-trailing-arm rear suspension, and Holden's own Red, Blue, and Black sixes and V8s. In 1986, the VL adopted the high-revving Nissan RB30 3.0L straight-six and legendary Turbo option. The 1988 VN introduced a widened body tailored specifically to Australian shoulder-room expectations and the rugged Buick-sourced 3.8L V6. The 2006 VE marked a monumental $1.03 billion investment creating the global GM Zeta rear-wheel-drive platform in Melbourne and Adelaide. The final Australian-built Commodore—a Red Hot VF II SS-V Redline sedan—rolled off the Elizabeth line on 20 October 2017.

kingswood.overview: The Holden Kingswood was Australia's definitive full-size family car and commercial workhorse from 1968 to 1985. Replacing the HR series with the all-new HK, the Kingswood moniker became an indelible piece of Australian cultural lexicon—celebrated in television ('Kingswood Country'), song, and outback folklore. Encompassing the budget Belmont, mainstream Kingswood, luxury Premier, sporty Monaro-derived options, surf-culture Sandman van/ute, and heavy-duty One Tonner cab-chassis, over 1.5 million examples were produced across HK, HT, HG, HQ, HJ, HX, HZ, and WB series.
kingswood.australian_market_notes: Introduced in 1968, the HK series brought the first V8s to Holden (imported Chevrolet 307ci V8) alongside new safety features like dual-circuit brakes and an energy-absorbing steering column. The 1969 HT introduced Holden's very own locally cast and machined V8s: the 253ci and 308ci Red V8s. The 1971 HQ was the single most successful automotive platform in Australian history, with 485,650 units built on an all-new full-perimeter front subframe chassis with coil springs on all four wheels. In 1977, the HZ series standardized Radial Tuned Suspension (RTS), giving the full-size car world-class European ride and cornering grip. The platform survived as the WB commercial range until 1985.

astra.overview: Spanning 36 years across seven generations, the Holden Astra was Holden's frontline small car. Launched in August 1984 as the LB/LC Astra, it originated as a badge-engineered Nissan Pulsar assembled in Clayton, Victoria. Under the Button Car Plan, the 1987 LD Astra combined Nissan body engineering with Holden's locally manufactured 1.6L and 1.8L Family II engines. In 1996, the Astra was reborn as the TR series, imported from Opel in Europe. The 1998 TS Astra became a massive commercial triumph, winning Wheels Car of the Year and spawning the hot hatch SRi and SRi Turbo (147 kW). The 2004 AH brought dynamic European styling and the 177 kW Astra VXR, followed by the PJ VXR coupe and the final high-tech 2016-2020 BK Astra hatchback (European Car of the Year) before Holden's retirement.
astra.australian_market_notes: The TS Astra was Holden's best-selling passenger car after the Commodore in the late 1990s and early 2000s, renowned for its vault-solid German body rigidity, standard dual airbags, and Lotus-tuned suspension. The sporty SRi and SRi Turbo models earned fierce cult status among hot hatch enthusiasts, while Bertone-styled Astra Convertibles brought accessible European glamour to Australian beaches.

ej-eh-hd-hr.overview: The 1962-1968 era represents the golden age of 1960s Holden dominance. The July 1962 EJ introduced clean, modern European-inspired styling, the milestone 1,000,000th Holden produced, and the prestigious Premier luxury model with standard automatic, leather bucket seats, and metallic paint. In August 1963, the legendary EH debuted Holden's all-new, world-class 'Red Motor' inline-six—featuring a 7-bearing crankshaft, hydraulic lifters, and 149ci (2.4L) and 179ci (2.9L) capacities. The EH became Australia's fastest-selling car ever, selling over 250,000 units in 18 months and claiming podium fame at Mount Panorama with the EH S4 Bathurst homologation special. The 1965 HD brought wider passenger accommodations and the twin-carburettor X2 engine, while the April 1966 HR resolved styling with crisp modern lines, front disc brakes, wider track, and the 186S engine with twin-barrel Bendix-Stromberg WW carburettor.
ej-eh-hd-hr.australian_market_notes: The introduction of the Red Motor in the EH transformed Holden's engineering standing worldwide, vastly outclassing Ford's Falcon sixes in thermal endurance and high-speed reliability. In 1966, the HR series pioneered critical Australian safety engineering with front lap-sash seatbelt mountings, padded dash, shatter-resistant mirror, and front disc brakes as an option (standard on Premier). Over 1,020,000 units were produced across the EJ, EH, HD, and HR models.

cruze.overview: The Holden Cruze nameplate lived two major chapters in Australia. First launched from 2002 to 2006 as the YG Cruze, it was an innovative subcompact all-wheel-drive crossover co-developed with Suzuki (based on the Ignis) featuring elevated ground clearance and 1.5L power. In 2009, Holden revived the name with the JG Cruze sedan. Most significantly, from March 2011 until October 2016, Holden invested over $1 billion to manufacture the JH Cruze Series II locally on a dedicated assembly line alongside the Commodore at Elizabeth, South Australia. The Australian-built Cruze featured an Australian-designed 5-door hatchback body style, local steering and suspension tuning, high-spec SRi and SRi-V turbo models (1.4L and 1.6L 132 kW turbos), and an efficient 2.0L Turbo Diesel. Over 125,000 Cruzes were built at Elizabeth.
cruze.australian_market_notes: The local production of the JH Cruze represented the return of small-car manufacturing to Australia for the first time since the 1990s. Holden's Melbourne design studio, led by Peter Hughes, penned the 5-door hatchback variant that was exported to world markets. Australian engineers recalibrated the suspension, dampers, and steering rack specifically for rough Australian rural bitumen, providing significantly superior composure compared to imported rivals.

sandman.overview: The Holden Sandman is the undisputed emblem of 1970s Australian youth and beach culture. Introduced in January 1974 on the HQ series (option package XX7 / XU3), the Sandman transformed humble commercial panel vans and utilities into vibrant, psychedelic recreational machines. Featuring bold side stripes, Monaro GTS sports dashboard with tachometer, GTS steering wheel, slotted steel rally wheels, twin bucket seats, and standard or optional 253ci and 308ci Red V8 power, the Sandman became a pop-culture legend closely tied to surfing, drive-in cinemas, and Australian freedom. While legally classified as commercial vehicles (saving buyers significant sales tax at the time), Sandmans were heavily optioned with sports suspensions, dual exhaust systems, customized shag-pile carpets, and tailgate mural art. In 1977, the HZ series bestowed Radial Tuned Suspension (RTS), giving the Sandman world-class handling dynamics.

adventra-crewman.overview: Developed during Holden's multi-million dollar engineering expansion under the VY/VZ Commodore program, the Adventra and Crewman represented audacious Australian engineering innovations. The 2003 Crewman was Australia's first locally designed and manufactured monocoque dual-cab utility, seating five adults on an extended 3,200 mm wheelbase with a heavy-duty leaf-sprung live rear axle capable of carrying up to a tonne. The Adventra was Holden's crossover all-wheel-drive sport wagon, boasting an Australian-engineered 'Cross-Trac' permanent AWD system (62% rear, 38% front torque split with automatic brake-traction management) and raised ground clearance. Holden combined the two concepts to create the monstrous Crewman Cross 8 and Cross 6, alongside V8 SS performance dual-cabs.
adventra-crewman.australian_market_notes: The Cross-Trac AWD system was developed entirely in-house by Holden engineers at Fishermans Bend and tested across the Simpson Desert and Mount Hotham snowfields. It delivered incredible off-road tractive ability without low-range gearing. The Crewman SS and Cross 8 became instant cult machines for tradies who wanted Monaro V8 thunder combined with family dual-cab practicality.

fe-fc-fb-ek.overview: The second and third generation post-war Holdens represented major leaps forward in Australian automotive engineering and design. Launched in July 1956, the FE introduced a completely modern, longer, lower body with wrap-around windscreen, 12-volt electrical architecture, recirculating ball steering, and Holden's very first factory station wagon—marketed as the 'Station Sedan'. The May 1958 FC refined the formula with an egg-crate grille and became the first car in Australian history to sell over 100,000 units in a calendar year. In January 1960, the FB adopted American fin-tail styling and a larger 138ci Grey motor, followed in May 1961 by the EK, which brought the historic introduction of the 3-speed Hydra-Matic automatic transmission to Holden. Across all four series, over 740,000 vehicles were built.
fe-fc-fb-ek.australian_market_notes: The FE-EK era cemented Holden's absolute supremacy in Australian motoring, securing over 50% total market share. The Station Sedan revolutionized family holidays and outback travel, while the EK Hydra-Matic made two-pedal driving accessible to middle Australia. The Dandenong (Victoria) assembly plant opened during the FE era to meet soaring national demand, while exports expanded across 46 overseas markets throughout Africa, Southeast Asia, and the Pacific.

torana.overview: The Holden Torana (derived from an Aboriginal word meaning 'to fly') is one of Australian motorsport's greatest legends. Starting in 1967 as a modified Vauxhall Viva four-cylinder compact (HB), the Torana evolved into a giant-killing six-cylinder weapon in the LC and LJ series, highlighted by Peter Brock's rainy 1972 Bathurst 500 victory in the triple-carburettor LJ GTR XU-1. The LH and LX generations made Australian automotive history as the only car platform engineered to accommodate 4-, 6-, and 8-cylinder engines, culminating in the Bathurst-dominating SL/R 5000 and A9X option pack.
torana.australian_market_notes: In 1969, Holden chief engineer George Roberts and designer Leo Pruneau stretched the LC Torana's nose by four inches to package the full-size Holden Red six-cylinder engine into a lightweight compact body, creating the GTR and Harry Firth's GTR XU-1. In 1974, the all-Australian LH series debuted, offering exceptional interior packaging and the thunderous 5.0L SL/R 5000 and L34 homologation packages. In 1976, the LX introduced the stunning three-door Hatchback body style and the immortal A9X option pack (rear disc brakes, Salisbury axle, rear-facing bonnet scoop), which Peter Brock and Jim Richards famously piloted to a crushing six-lap victory at the 1979 Bathurst 1000, setting a lap record on the final lap.

monaro.overview: The Holden Monaro is Australia's most revered two-door muscle car and grand tourer. Introduced in July 1968 with the HK series, the pillarless hardtop coupe captured national imagination by winning the 1968 Bathurst 500 on debut with Bruce McPhee and Barry Mulholland in a GTS 327, followed by Colin Bond's win in the 1969 HT GTS 350. Resurrected thirty-three years later following a sensational reception as the 'Coupe 22' concept at the 1998 Sydney Motor Show, the modern V2 and VZ Monaro CV8 captivated enthusiasts globally and was exported to North America as the Pontiac GTO and the UK as the Vauxhall Monaro.

The HQ series brought softer, more organic proportions, offering the GTS 350 and introducing the 4-door GTS sedan in 1973. The modern rebirth engineered by Mike Simcoe in 2001 (V2/VZ) utilized the VT/VX Commodore platform, packing the 5.7L LS1 V8 and supercharged V6, before culminating in the twin-hood-scoop 2005 CV8-Z.

48-215.overview: The Holden 48-215 (retrospectively referred to as the 'FX') was Australia's first mass-produced domestic motor vehicle, famously unveiled on 29 November 1948 by Prime Minister Ben Chifley with the words: 'She's a beauty!'. Developed under GM Project 2000, it combined American interior room and robust unibody construction with European operating economy, tailored specifically for Australia's harsh corrugated roads. In January 1951, the 50-2106 Coupe Utility was launched, defining the iconic Australian 'ute', followed in July 1953 by the 48-215-257 Business Sedan for taxi operators. Over 120,402 examples were produced.
48-215.australian_market_notes: The 48-215 introduced unitary (monocoque) construction to Australian volume manufacturing, eliminating heavy separate chassis rails while providing extraordinary torsional rigidity. Powered by the legendary 132.5ci (2.16L) overhead valve 'Grey Motor' inline-six, it easily outperformed British four-cylinder rivals in hill-climbing, highway cruising, and reliability. Customer demand was so overwhelming that waiting lists stretched out past two years, establishing Holden's 70-year reign over Australian automotive culture.

jackaroo.name: Holden Jackaroo
jackaroo.overview: The Holden Jackaroo (Isuzu Trooper / Bighorn) was Holden's frontline heavy-duty four-wheel-drive wagon from 1981 to 2004. Engineered to conquer the Australian outback, the Jackaroo competed directly against the Toyota LandCruiser Prado, Mitsubishi Pajero, and Nissan Patrol. The first-generation UBS-1 (1981-1992) offered short and long wheelbase bodies with rugged four-cylinder petrol and diesel engines. The second-generation UBS-2 (1992-2004) expanded into a wide-body luxury family 4WD featuring coil-sprung rear suspension, shift-on-the-fly 4WD, potent 3.2L and 3.5L DOHC 24V V6 petrol engines (158 kW), and advanced 3.0L 4JX1 common-rail turbo-diesel. The flagship Monterey added leather trim, woodgrain, climate control, and heated seats.
jackaroo.australian_market_notes: The Jackaroo earned widespread admiration for its exceptional interior room, expansive glasshouse visibility, and compliant ride over outback corrugations. In 1993, legendary Australian rally driver Peter Brock competed in the Australian Safari behind the wheel of an Isuzu/Holden Jackaroo, demonstrating its extreme durability. The 3.5L V6 Monterey was regarded as one of the best-value luxury tow vehicles of its era.

colorado.name: Holden Colorado
colorado.overview: The Holden Colorado was Holden's rugged 4x4 and 4x2 dual-cab, space-cab, and single-cab workhorse pick-up, replacing the legendary Rodeo in 2008. Across the RC and RG generations, the Colorado delivered class-leading 3.5-tonne braked towing capacity and up to 500Nm of torque from its Duramax 2.8L turbo-diesel engine. In 2016, Holden's engineering team at Lang Lang conducted a massive Australian-specific chassis, steering, and powertrain calibration that transformed refinement and dynamics.
colorado.australian_market_notes: The RC generation was built in Rayong, Thailand alongside the Isuzu D-Max, powered by the bulletproof 3.0L Isuzu 4JJ1-TC turbo-diesel and Holden's Australian-built 3.6L Alloytec V6. The RG series (launched in 2012 on GM's global mid-size truck platform) introduced the potent 2.8L Duramax diesel. The 2016 RG Series II introduced a Centrifugal Pendulum Absorber (CPA) torque converter—a first in the dual-cab ute segment—damping engine vibrations and enabling earlier torque converter lock-up. Range topped by the Z71 and HSV SportsCat.
